minutes.headline: School Committee approved four school improvement plans and posting of student custodian jobs, then went into executive session.
minutes.summary: Remote meeting. The committee heard the superintendent's report on Turkey Hill air quality, enrollment and remote learning, then the four principals presented school improvement plans, which were approved. It also approved posting student custodian positions, named MASC delegates, accepted charter school reports, and heard a survey summary and quarter-two learning-model change requests. It ended by voting to enter executive session for union negotiation strategy, not to return.

attendees.role: interim director of teaching and learning

public_comment.topic: Concern about cleanliness gap between teacher and parent survey views, teacher well-being, and the primary school's reading program.

votes.motion: Approve minutes of the September 2nd and September 16th regular session meetings.
Approve the four school improvement plans as presented.
Approve permission to post the student custodian positions as described.
Nominate the chair as voting MASC delegate and Ms. Archambault as alternate.
Accept the annual reports from the Parker and Sizer charter schools.
Go into executive session for union negotiation strategy, not to return to public meeting, and adjourn immediately after.

Projected cost is paid partly from the COVID relief grant and the custodial account, with the balance absorbed into the local budget after January 1. Possible FY22 budget item.

what_happened.line: The School Committee approved all four school improvement plans as presented, 5-0 by roll call.
It voted 5-0 to post student custodian positions; the business manager will evaluate them and put them on the FY22 budget list.
The committee named its MASC delegate and alternate and accepted the Parker and Sizer charter school annual reports, each 5-0.
The superintendent reported that October 1 enrollment sets state funding, and that superintendents are urging a hold-harmless for FY22.
Quarter-two learning-model change requests were shared with the bus contractor, and routes may be adjusted. The meeting ended in executive session on union negotiation strategy.

why_it_matters: The student custodian positions are paid partly from one-time COVID relief money and the custodial account, and the balance moves into the local budget after January 1, so they may become a recurring FY22 cost.
State funding follows October 1 enrollment, so a rise in homeschooling and any hold-harmless decision for FY22 affect how much state aid the schools receive.
watch_next: The FY22 budget list, for the student custodian positions and any integrated math textbook purchase.
State action on a hold-harmless for FY22 school funding, and the end-of-December deadline for spending town CARES funds.
